priceEarningsRatio.interpretation: A low P/E (< 15) suggests the stock is cheap; a high P/E (> 30) indicates it may be expensive or over-valued.

rules.comment: The P/E ratio of {value} suggests the stock is cheap relative to earnings.
The P/E ratio of {value} is fairly typical.
The P/E ratio of {value} indicates the stock is relatively expensive compared to its earnings.

earningsPerShare.interpretation: Higher EPS means greater profitability per share.

rules.comment: The EPS of {value} is low; profitability may be a concern.
The EPS of {value} shows modest profitability.
The EPS of {value} is a strong indicator of the company's profitability.

dividendYield.interpretation: Shows how much cash-flow an investor receives from dividends relative to the stock price.

rules.comment: The dividend yield of {value}% is lower than the market average.
The dividend yield of {value}% is around the market norm.
The dividend yield of {value}% is attractive for income-focused investors.

marketCap.interpretation: Measures the size of the company; e.g., $2.3 trillion is a very large (large-cap) firm.

rules.comment: The market cap of ${value/trillion} trillion makes it one of the world's giants.
The market cap of ${value/trillion} trillion indicates a very large, stable company.
The market capitalization of ${value/trillion} trillion indicates a sizable player.

debtToEquityRatio.interpretation: Indicates the degree of financial leverage. A moderate ratio (approximately 1) is typical; higher values imply more debt risk.

rules.comment: The debt-to-equity ratio of {value} suggests very little leverage.
The debt-to-equity ratio of {value} suggests a moderate level of leverage.
The debt-to-equity ratio of {value} indicates high leverage; watch for risk.

returnOnEquity.interpretation: Shows how efficiently the company turns equity into profit. Higher percentages are better.

rules.comment: The ROE of {pct}% is below average.
The ROE of {pct}% is healthy.
The ROE of {pct}% is very strong, showing efficient profit generation.

returnOnAssets.interpretation: Measures profitability relative to all assets employed. Higher values indicate better asset utilisation.

rules.comment: The ROA of {pct}% is modest.
The ROA of {pct}% indicates efficient asset utilization.
The ROA of {pct}% is excellent, showing superb asset productivity.

currentRatio.interpretation: Assesses short-term liquidity. A ratio above 1 means the firm can cover its short-term obligations.

rules.comment: The current ratio of {value} signals potential short-term liquidity issues.
The current ratio of {value} suggests the company has a good short-term liquidity position.
The current ratio of {value} indicates a very comfortable liquidity cushion.

quickRatio.interpretation: A stricter liquidity test; values >= 1 suggest the firm can meet immediate liabilities without relying on inventory.

rules.comment: The quick ratio of {value} may be insufficient for immediate obligations.
The quick ratio of {value} indicates a strong ability to meet short-term obligations.
The quick ratio of {value} shows an exceptionally strong liquidity position.

bookValuePerShare.interpretation: Represents the net asset value attributable to each share; useful as a floor valuation.

rules.comment: The book value per share of {value} is a measure of the company's net asset value on a per-share basis.
